learning_outcomes.text: Students will acquire a unified vision of Materials Science (MS), through the knowledge and understanding of its fundamental principles and concepts.
They will understand the importance of the structure-properties relationship as a guiding principle for any activity related to the use and/or development of materials in Engineering.
They will be able to apply the acquired knowledge to solve problems and questions related to MS, as well as to correctly interpret the obtained results.

They will develop the basic skills necessary to operate in MS laboratories, and the capacities for critical reasoning and autonomous learning, as well as for consulting bibliography and using software, databases, etc., related to MS, familiarizing themselves with the main terminology related to MS in English.

syllabus_topics: The Science and Engineering of Materials
Introduction to Materials Science and Engineering
Structure of metallic and ceramic materials
Description of the Bravais lattice. The unit cell
The 14 Bravais lattices. The 7 crystal systems
Miller notation. Positions, directions, and planes in the lattice
Mechanical properties: Deformation, restoration, and recrystallization
Elastic deformation. Modulus of elasticity and Poisson's ratio
Plastic deformation. Yield strength, tensile strength, ductility, and toughness
Deformation of single crystals. Schmid's Law
Phase Diagrams. Development of equilibrium microstructures
Fundamental definitions and concepts of Phase Diagrams
Phase diagrams. Pure systems and binary systems
Diagrams with intermediate compounds and phases
Diagrams with eutectoid and peritectoid points
Fe-C phase diagram. Heat treatments of steels
Kinetics of phase transformations. Nucleation and growth
Isothermal transformations of austenite. TTT curves
Heat treatments of steels: normalizing, annealing, quenching, and tempering
Laboratory Practice 1: Preparation, observation, and microstructural characterization of materials
Laboratory Practice 2: Mechanical characterization of materials. Tensile and hardness tests
Laboratory Practice 3: Electrical characterization of materials. Electrical conductivity
Computer practice: Use of software for graphic representation and data analysis

assessment_methods.method: Final theoretical/practical exam and/or partial cumulative and/or eliminatory exams
Utilization of practical activities carried out in: classroom, laboratory, computer room, field, visits, etc.
Resolution and submission of activities (cases, problems, reports, assignments, projects, etc.), individually and/or in groups

assessment_rules: There are two evaluation paths: continuous evaluation and global evaluation. In the continuous evaluation (ordinary call), the final theoretical/practical exam accounts for 70%, a questionnaire on practical activities for 10%, and two continuous assessment activities (problem-solving) for 20%. The final exam requires a minimum of 2/4 points in the theoretical block, 2.5/6 points in the practical exercises block, and an overall minimum of 5/10 points to pass the course. The practical activities questionnaire and continuous assessment activities are non-recoverable. In the global evaluation, a theoretical/practical exam accounts for 80% and a questionnaire related to practical activities accounts for 20%. The same minimum scores apply to the exam in the global evaluation. For extraordinary calls (November, June/July), the final grade is the sum of scores obtained in the non-recoverable activities from the previous course and a new theoretical/practical exam, which has the same structure and weighting (70%) as in the ordinary call.
